title: Alfresco records document events but not the business decision behind them
content:
Alfresco's audit surface is document-shaped. It records versions, uploads and moves — the events that happen to a file. What it does not record is the business decision: who accepted this, under which rule, and what the state was before the acceptance.

The distinction is not pedantic, because the two are routinely conflated in practice. A document management system that shows a new version at 14:03 by a named user looks like an audit trail until someone asks what that version *meant*. Version n+1 may be an approval, a typo fix, or a rollback, and the repository cannot tell them apart. The prior state that the decision was taken against is likewise absent — versions record the after, not the before-and-because.

For the seven Alfresco partners carrying this finding, the value is that the gap sits in the part of the client's estate they already own and operate. They are not being asked to replace the repository or to argue against it; they are being asked to record something the repository was never designed to hold, which is a smaller and more defensible claim to take to their own customers.
